title: The Weir Line
premise: A crane operator's death gets filed as a weather accident. His sister won't sign off on that, and pulling the thread means dragging a street kid's salvage, a nurse's off-book list, an analyst's own model, and a guard's buried report up out of Sump Row and into the boardroom that scheduled the cut that killed him.

roles.persona: Blunt, runs out of patience before she runs out of words. Keeps every one of her brother Sable's shift logs since their mother died. Wants a name on the accident, not a weather pattern; fears grief with no name attached just becomes weather too; would never take a payout that reads like a price on him.

Fast, transactional, softens once trust is earned. Found a company drive in the same debris that took Sable Voss. Wants it out of his hands before whoever wants it back finds out he has it; fears being the kind of story the Sump forgets by winter; would never hand it over for free until someone asks him right.

Tired, exact, no wasted words. Treats execs by day for a wage and Sump Row's dock workers off the books after hours for nothing, keeping a private list of the drowned-sounding lungs the official chart has no room for. Wants the list to matter to someone with the power to act on it; fears it disappearing with her, unread.

Precise, then suddenly plain when the precision runs out. Wrote the ration model and signed off on the week's anomalous cut without reading past the summary line. Wants to find out the cut was a coincidence; fears finding out it was not more than she fears losing the job that pays for that fear.

Flat and procedural until it isn't. Filed the maintenance report the night Sable Voss died and was told by morning it never existed, but kept his own copy. Wants the report on record with his own name on it; fears losing the pension that keeps his mother housed in Sump Row; would never destroy the copy.

Measured, turns statements into questions so the room agrees for her. Grew up in Sump Row before marrying onto the Aurelian Hydro board, and signed the memo that let the company cut the ration early to protect the quarter. Wants to be right about the memo; fears her own signature more than she fears the drowned.

items.name: Sable's drive
items.description: Kip's find, but really Sable's: a company data drive, cracked but readable, pulled from the same debris pile that took him. Whoever holds it holds the last thing he saw.

items.name: Doc Mira's list
items.description: Doc Mira Chen's off-book ledger of dock workers treated for the same drowned-sounding cough, kept because the clinic's real chart has no room for them. To her it means the pattern predates Sable by months.

items.name: the redirection schedule
items.description: The pattern read off Aurelian Hydro's own maintenance drones: power pulled from the Sump Row storm pumps on a fixed schedule that lines up with every low-tide cut. To Talis it means the model wasn't wrong, it was obeyed.

items.name: Cross's copy
items.description: The maintenance report Cross Ivanov filed the night Sable Voss died, power log and signature included, kept in a locker he isn't supposed to still have a key to. To him it means somebody besides the family already knew.

items.name: Ilona's own words
items.description: What Ilona Vale said over dinner at Zenith Dining when she thought the booth beside her was empty: that she signed the redirection knowing what it would cost the low tide. To her it is the one sentence she can never unsay.

facts.text: He counted every lift out loud. Four containers, one gantry, no surprises. The report doesn't have a single one of his words in it.
I've got eleven names on that list who came in with the same drowned cough inside a year. The clinic's chart has room for zero of them.
I signed off on the summary line. I never read the redirection table underneath it. I don't think anyone above me did either.
I told legal there was no name attached to the anomaly. That was true for about six hours.
My mother's in a Sump Row block that floods on the same schedule. I filed that report for her as much as for him.
Found it wedged in the same debris as the body. Didn't feel right to sell something that came up with him.

acts.title: The Weir Line Breaks
acts.summary: An accident becomes a question the family won't let close.

acts.title: Behind the Glass
acts.summary: The question climbs into the company that authored the answer.

acts.title: The Ledger and the Board
acts.summary: The abstraction gets a voice, overheard and undeniable.

acts.title: The Choice
acts.summary: The case is complete; what's left is who gets to hold it.

narrative.description: Petra Moss corners you before you've even finished asking about her brother, a folder of shift logs already in her hand, like she's been waiting for someone new enough to the district to still ask questions.
narrative.playerHint: Hear Petra out about her brother.
narrative.stake: It's not weather, and if she says that to one more precinct wall she's going to put her fist through it. If nobody outside the Sump believes her, Sable goes in the ground as a footnote.

narrative.description: Kip Thorn works the stalls at Dredge Feed like he owns the block, but he goes quiet and pulls you aside the second Petra's name comes up, describing exactly where the flood left something worth more than he wants to be caught holding.
narrative.playerHint: Talk to Kip about what the tide left behind.
narrative.stake: He's not selling this one, but he's not holding it either. Whoever the drive belongs to at Aurelian Hydro will come looking for it, and Kip would rather it be gone from his hands than in them when they do.

narrative.description: Right where Kip said, wedged under a loose stall board at Dredge Feed, the drive is still tangled in the same debris the tide never fully gave back.
narrative.playerHint: Pick up the drive Kip pointed you to.
narrative.stake: It's the only piece of Sable that survived the water. Leaving it there means leaving him a rumor instead of a record.

narrative.description: Doc Mira Chen meets you in the storage room behind the Vitalis Spire Clinic, off the clock and off the chart, and lays out a list of names that all drowned the same way Sable did, just slower.
narrative.playerHint: Talk to Doc Mira at the clinic.
narrative.stake: She's kept this list for a year with nowhere to put it. If it dies with her it was never anything but a private grief; if it reaches someone who can act, it's evidence.

narrative.description: You find Talis Rook at Oxide Filter, the one counter close enough to Aurelian Hydro that she trusts it, and set the cracked drive on the table between the two full cups she never finished.
narrative.playerHint: Show Talis the drive.
narrative.stake: She wrote the model. If the drive is what it looks like, she signed something she never actually read, and she has to decide whether that's still just math.

narrative.description: Talis asks you to watch the Glass Apex skyline from street level while she watches the same feed from her desk, so neither of them is trusting the dashboard alone.
narrative.playerHint: Observe the Glass Apex district for the drone pattern.
narrative.stake: Six drones over the district at an hour nothing should be flying, redirecting power away from the storm pumps. She needs it confirmed by a second pair of eyes before she'll believe her own model.

narrative.description: Cross Ivanov meets you at Apex Oversight after shift change, the lockers lit by one working tube, and pulls a folder out of a locker his badge shouldn't still open.
narrative.playerHint: Talk to Cross at Apex Oversight.
narrative.stake: He's kept this report for months without a place to put it. Handing it over costs him the pension that keeps his mother housed, but keeping it costs him the one rule he hasn't broken yet.

narrative.description: Knowing the redirection schedule, you're in the next booth at Zenith Dining at exactly the hour Ilona Vale takes her board lunch, close enough to hear her explain the numbers to a colleague who never has to ask twice.
narrative.playerHint: Listen to Ilona Vale and Talis Rook at Zenith Dining.
narrative.stake: Talis needs to hear Ilona say it herself before she'll turn the model's evidence against the company paying her. What Ilona says over lunch is the difference between a coincidence and a confession.

narrative.description: You lay the drive, the list, the schedule, the report and the overheard confession across the counter at Apex Oversight, and Cross Ivanov reads every page aloud until the desk sergeant has no choice but to write it down.
narrative.playerHint: Give everything to Cross and put the case on record.
narrative.stake: This is the report Cross wanted to file the night it happened. It ends his pension and starts the inquiry Petra has been asking for since the funeral.

narrative.description: You bring everything to Ilona Vale at Aurelian Hydro instead, and she doesn't deny a word of it, just names a figure that would lift Petra's whole block above the flood line if the file closes quietly.
narrative.playerHint: Bring everything to Ilona and hear her offer.
narrative.stake: Ilona wants this to disappear at a price that looks enough like justice that nobody has to call it a bribe. It buys Sump Row real relief and buries Sable's name at the same time.

endings.title: On the Record
endings.epilogue: Cross Ivanov reads the whole case into the precinct log until someone writes it down, and loses his pension inside the week for it. Petra Moss gets a name on the file at last, not weather. Talis Rook is called before an inquiry she does not try to avoid. Ilona Vale goes back to Sump Row exactly once, in a car that does not wait for her, and the ration schedule changes before the next low tide, not because anyone forgave her, but because now everyone is watching.

endings.title: The Payout
endings.epilogue: Ilona Vale comes down from the Glass Apex herself and offers Petra Moss a number that would move her whole block above the flood line, no admission attached, no name on any form. "That's a lot of money for a weather event," Petra says. "I know exactly what it was," Ilona answers, the first sentence she has spoken all year that doesn't end like a question. The block gets rebuilt three floors higher. Sable Voss stays filed as an accident forever, and nobody who watches Petra sign the papers thinks she made the wrong choice.

title: Last Call at Oxide Filter
premise: A barista who has poured the same order for two years starts noticing what her regular writes on the cups she never finishes, and has to decide what to do with someone else's guilt before building security decides for her.

roles.persona: Quiet, precise with drink orders, reads people by what they order and never finish. Wants someone she can trust to see what she's been saving; fears being the one whose name is on the sweep report; would never just throw the cups away.
Precise until the precision runs out. Orders the same coffee every day and leaves it to go cold when the numbers she's reading won't leave her alone.
Runs the confiscation sweep on a fixed rotation and thinks paper cups with handwriting on them are somebody else's problem the moment they're bagged.

items.name: the rotation window
items.description: Denna's read on when the confiscation bin sits unwatched between the guard's rounds. To her it's the only chance the cups have of coming back before they're read by the wrong people.

items.name: the cup notes
items.description: A fistful of paper cups with Talis Rook's own numbers and dates scrawled on them, saved by Denna instead of thrown out. To Talis they are the doubt she has never once said out loud.

facts.text: You learn who's about to break by what they stop finishing. Talis stopped finishing her coffee the same week she stopped finishing sentences.

acts.title: The Counter
acts.summary: Denna notices the pattern and needs a reason to trust someone with it.

acts.title: The Recovery
acts.summary: What security took has to come back before the wrong people read it.

narrative.description: Denna waves you toward a corner table at Oxide Filter during the one slow hour of her shift, when the lobby traffic thins out enough that nobody is counting who talks to who.
narrative.playerHint: Go to Oxide Filter during the slow hour.
narrative.stake: She is not saying a word about this over a full counter. If you show up at the wrong hour she loses her nerve and the cups stay wherever they've ended up.

narrative.description: Denna tells you about the cups while she steams milk for someone else, never looking up, describing exactly how a security sweep swept her savings into a confiscation bin along with the lobby's other unclaimed paper.
narrative.playerHint: Hear Denna out about the cups.
narrative.stake: She has been saving evidence of somebody else's doubt for weeks with no plan for it. Saying it out loud to you is the first risk she has taken since she started saving them.

narrative.description: You watch the lobby floor from a mezzanine seat long enough to clock the guard's rounds, the gap between when the bin gets checked and when it gets moved.
narrative.playerHint: Observe the Glass Apex district to learn the rotation.
narrative.stake: Guessing wrong means walking into the sweep in progress. Denna needs the window, not a guess, before the bin gets emptied for good.

narrative.description: In the gap Denna's window gave you, you lift the bagged cups out of the confiscation bin while the floor guard is two corridors away on his fixed round.
narrative.playerHint: Take the cup notes before the sweep report goes upstairs.
narrative.stake: Once the sweep report is filed with Denna's name on it, the cups become a disciplinary case instead of a coffee order. This is the only window that closes it clean.

narrative.description: You set the recovered cups on the counter in front of Talis Rook, who recognizes her own handwriting before she recognizes what it means that someone else read it first.
narrative.playerHint: Give the cup notes back to Talis.
narrative.stake: Nobody has ever shown Talis proof of her own doubt before. What she does with it now is hers, but she can't pretend she never wrote it.

endings.title: Kept in the Apron
endings.epilogue: You put the cups back in Talis Rook's hands at her own counter, stained and unexplained. She never asks where they went. She orders it the same way the next morning, black, too hot to drink, and lets it go cold for a different reason this time.

title: Signal Under Sump Row
premise: A street kid who fished a company drive out of the flood finds something stranger in the same water: a junction box quietly stealing power from the district's own storm pumps, and needs a maintenance tech willing to look at it instead of look away.

roles.persona: Fast, transactional, softens once trust is earned. Wants a witness who won't cash a good find in cheap; fears sitting on something worth more than his life; would never let this one go for less than its actual weight.

Talks like he's still reading a schematic, careful, methodical. Wants a reason to look at a junction he's never been cleared to open; fears what he already suspects it's doing to his mother's block more than he fears his own shift log.

items.name: the spare hatch key
items.description: A maintenance key Kip won't say how he got, cut for a hatch nobody's supposed to open off-shift. Means the only way into the junction that doesn't ask questions first.

items.name: the routing reading
items.description: What Wick reads off the junction box: power meant for the Sump Row storm pumps, routed elsewhere on a schedule that matches every low-tide cut this year. To him it means the redirection has a shape now, not just a rumor.

facts.text: I don't report what's in those tunnels because the people I'd report it to are the reason it's down there.

acts.title: The Tip
acts.summary: Kip needs someone who won't just sell the story cheap to see the junction for what it is.

acts.title: The Tunnel
acts.summary: Getting close to the box costs access nobody hands out for free.

narrative.description: Kip waves you down at Dredge Feed before you've even cleared the flooded stairwell, too excited to haggle for once.
narrative.playerHint: Go find Kip at Dredge Feed.
narrative.stake: He has found something he cannot price on his own, and he would rather show it to a witness than describe it to a buyer who might not believe him.

narrative.description: Kip describes a junction box still humming under the drained floodwater, feeding a line that isn't on any map he's ever traded for, and presses a spare hatch key into your hand before he can talk himself out of it.
narrative.playerHint: Hear Kip out and take the spare key.
narrative.stake: He needs the box read by someone who understands wiring, not sold to someone who understands buyers. The key is the only way in that doesn't announce itself.

narrative.description: You use the spare key to pick up an unrostered maintenance shift out of the Harbor Junction office, the easiest way to be standing near the overnight hatch without anyone asking why.
narrative.playerHint: Work a maintenance shift to get near the hatch.
narrative.stake: Wick cannot get near that junction without an official reason, and neither can you. A shift nobody questions is the only access that doesn't get reported before you've even opened the panel.

narrative.description: Inside the hatch, Wick reads the junction's routing twice before he'll say it out loud, his hands shaking less from the cold than from what the numbers mean for the six blocks over his own mother's flat.
narrative.playerHint: Talk to Wick about what the junction is doing.
narrative.stake: He is the only one who can make this reading mean something instead of just look strange. Saying it to you out loud is the first time he has said it to anyone.

narrative.description: You bring the reading back to Kip at Dredge Feed, and for once he doesn't ask what it's worth before he asks what it means.
narrative.playerHint: Bring the routing reading back to Kip.
narrative.stake: This is the first fact he has ever held that has a name attached instead of a price. He finally has something worth more than a sale.

endings.title: A Fact With a Name On It
endings.epilogue: Wick writes the routing down for Kip plainly, the way he'd write a repair order, and doesn't take it up his own chain, because his chain is the reason it's down there unreported. Kip finally has something worth more than a sale: a fact with a name on it, and someone who already believes him.

title: The Exchange Rate
premise: A mall vendor's grey-market ration chit turns out to be stolen from a batch that was supposed to be destroyed, and when the man who tipped her off to it collapses in her queue, she and the transit agent who caught the serial have to get him help before they decide who's to blame.

roles.persona: Prices anything in a second, never asks what it's for, until she has to. Wants a fair price and no questions; fears the batch being traced to her stall; would never leave a customer to collapse over a chit she sold him.

Checks serials twice out of habit, not suspicion, until the habit finds something real. Wants to know what he actually bought for his mother; fears finding out he's been funding the exact thing he's supposed to catch.

items.name: the ration chit
items.description: A grey-market water ration top-up with a serial that matches a batch logged as destroyed three weeks ago. To Milo it means the batch never actually left circulation.

items.name: the stim kit
items.description: The emergency kit Yara keeps under her counter for exactly this kind of collapse. To her it's the difference between an ambulance that asks questions and a clinic that doesn't.

items.name: the batch reading
items.description: What the chit's serial actually traces to once Milo runs it against the transit log. To him it means a route through the tunnels, not just a stolen object.

facts.text: Got my stall license off a man who owed my mother a favor and never learned my name. I've been pricing things fast ever since so nobody has to ask twice.

acts.title: The Stall
acts.summary: A chit that shouldn't exist changes what Milo thought he was buying.

acts.title: The Reckoning
acts.summary: Someone pays for the batch before anyone can decide who's guilty.

narrative.description: Yara Fenn waves you over to her stall at the Sump Exchange mall between customers, sizing you up for a sale before you've said a word.
narrative.playerHint: Go to Yara Fenn's stall at Sump Exchange.
narrative.stake: She has got a queue and no patience for browsers. If you don't come to her, she is not chasing you down to explain what's wrong with the chit she just sold.

narrative.description: Yara slides a ration chit and a battered stim kit across the counter in the same motion, already talking about the next customer before you've finished asking where the chit came from.
narrative.playerHint: Talk to Yara about the chit.
narrative.stake: She needs this batch moved before anyone traces the serials back to her stall, and she'd rather you be the one holding both the chit and the means to fix what it might cost someone.

narrative.description: Milo Draeger takes one look at the chit's serial at his Harbor Junction booth and pulls up the transit log without a word, checking it twice the way he checks everything.
narrative.playerHint: Show the chit to Milo at the Harbor Junction booth.
narrative.stake: He bought one of these for his own mother without checking. Now he needs to know exactly what he paid for before he decides what to do about it.

narrative.description: Word reaches you that the dock worker who tipped Yara off to the batch has collapsed in her queue, chit still in his fist, and you get the stim kit to the Vitalis Spire Clinic's after-hours intake before anyone has to call it an emergency.
narrative.playerHint: Deliver the stim kit to the Vitalis Spire Clinic.
narrative.stake: Yara would rather explain a delivery than an ambulance report. Getting the kit there fast is the difference between a patient and a case number.

narrative.description: Back at his booth, Milo looks at the batch reading you brought him and starts logging serials into a personal notebook instead of just the transit system.
narrative.playerHint: Talk to Milo about the batch reading.
narrative.stake: He nearly funded the exact circulation he is supposed to catch. Whatever he does with the reading now decides whether that habit means anything.

endings.title: Treated, Not Told
endings.epilogue: The collapsed worker gets treated after hours at the Vitalis Spire Clinic by a nurse who never asks for a name. Yara never learns where the batch really came from. Milo starts checking serial numbers on everything he buys for his mother, not just the one that already burned him.
